title: Direct image and finite Tor amplitude
statement:
Fix an algebraically closed field $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type morphism (separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]). Use the ordinary derived categories of modules over the constant ring sheaves on the small étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site; def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and the module-sheaf derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

Assume a fixed integer $N\geq0$ satisfies the uniform vanishing condition, denoted here by $\operatorname{UDV}(f,A;N)$:
$$
R^rf_*M=0\quad\text{for every sheaf }M\text{ of }A_X\text{-modules and every integer }r>N.
$$
This displayed predicate is imposed for the present field $k$.

Let $a\leq b$ be integers and $K\in D^b_c(X_{\Et},A)$ a bounded constructible complex [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude]: for every sheaf $M$ of $A_X$-modules in degree zero, $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^L M)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$, with the ordinary étale derived tensor of [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Then $Rf_*K\in D^b_c(Y_{\Et},A)$ and $Rf_*K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+N]$.

proof.text: The coefficient conventions [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] give the extended absolute value on $E$ and $\mathfrak m_E=(\varpi_E)$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $\mathcal O_E$ is a DVR with finite residue field; [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] therefore makes $A$ a finite local ring with maximal ideal generated by the image $\bar\varpi_E$ of $\varpi_E$. Write $\kappa=A/(\bar\varpi_E)$. The ring $A$ is Noetherian: every ideal is a finite set and hence is generated by its elements. Since the absolute value extends the $\ell$-adic one, $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$, whence $\ell\in\mathfrak m_E=(\varpi_E)$, and $\ell^n\in(\varpi_E^n)$. Thus $\ell^n A=0$. The integer $\ell^n$ is invertible in $k$ because $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$.

source.place: Proof, fourth paragraph (finite invertible-exponent coefficients); coefficient arithmetic written explicitly.

proof.text: Put L=K tensor^L kappa_X. The Tor-amplitude hypothesis gives cohomology vanishing outside [a,b], hence L.IsGE a and L.IsLE b by the standard derived t-structure characterization.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph (residue-field tensor concentration); Tor amplitude: Stacks 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude, sites-cohomology.tex.

proof.text: The existing ordinary module-sheaf direct image has additive, left-exact and Grothendieck-abelian category instances from the upstream framework. Convert the assumed vanishing of H^q(Rf_*(S[0])) for q>N to classical right-derived vanishing by Functor.isZero_rightDerived_of_isZero_homology. Apply [lem-etale-derived-functor-upper-amplitude] with d=N.toNat to L.IsLE b. Left t-exactness gives the lower bound a. Since N>=0, the resulting upper bound b+N.toNat is b+N. The separately stated module-sheaf comparison theorems are not used.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph (direct-image cohomological bound), implemented by Stacks 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived, (4)(c); module categories: Stacks 03DA, 03DB, 03EW; left exact direct image: Stacks 071J.

proof.text: Step 1 proves that $A$ is finite and annihilated by an integer $\ell^n$ invertible in $k$. The schemes $X,Y$ are finite type over the field $k$, and $K$ is bounded constructible by hypothesis. Thus [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] applies and gives $F:=Rf_*K\in D^b_c(Y_{\Et},A)$. This establishes the bounded constructibility clause and the hypothesis needed for the residue test below.

The residue module kappa is a quotient of the finite ring A, hence finite. Over the Noetherian ring A it is finitely presented. Bounded constructibility of K gives an upper cohomological bound. Apply [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant] to identify Rf_*K tensor^L kappa_Y with Rf_*(K tensor^L kappa_X). Transport the vanishing from Step 3 along this isomorphism and the homology functor.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph (finite-presentation projection formula). Canonical map: Stacks 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map, sites-cohomology.tex; the stronger finitely-presented coefficient result is the cited DAG lemma, not an application of the perfect-coefficient lemma 0944.

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-residue-tor-test] to F=Rf_*K, its bounded constructibility from Step 4, and its residue-tensor vanishing from Step 5. This gives Tor amplitude [a,b+N], completing both conclusions.

source.place: Proof, final sentence (residue-field criterion); Tor-amplitude convention: Stacks 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude, sites-cohomology.tex.
